summary: Peer GPU contention causing sustained p95 latency spikes and request timeouts in dedicated pool pool-rtp-03
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 07:40 UTC, Scriptly AI reported elevated p95 (~3.2s -> 7.8s) and intermittent 504/502 timeouts when calling our hosted endpoints backed by their dedicated pool (pool-rtp-03). Impact: customer-facing inference degraded for ~90 minutes; streaming sessions dropped; retries caused 429 bursts. Environment: dedicated pool pool-rtp-03, node group gpu-a100-1, region us-west-2. Observed behaviour: p95/p99 spikes coincident with high variance in request cost (mix of long-seq summarization and many short chat queries). Autoscaler config had min_replicas=1 and aggressive scale_up_threshold=0.85 leading to sustained high per-GPU utilization and head-of-line queueing. Expected behaviour: stable p95 < 800ms and no 5xx for in-reservation traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a steady mix of long-sequence (seq_len ~ 4096) and short chat (seq_len ~ 128) requests at 350 rps against the model pinned in pool-rtp-03. 2) Observe per-GPU scheduler queue depth and token throughput. 3) Notice serialization on single CUDA stream and elevated GPU context-switches when long and short jobs overlap. 4) Retries from clients increase queue depth and surface 429/504s.
metrics_snapshot: From Grafana dashboard: p50=210ms p95=3.2s (spike to 7.8s at peak) p99=12.1s; GPU util per-card: 92% average with 1 card at 99% bursting; CUDA context-switches increased 8x; inference RPS fell by 38% relative to baseline. Queue length at the runtime RPC layer jumped from 4 -> 26. API gateway 429 rate jumped to 18%.

investigation_notes: 07:45 UTC - Support triage: validated customer traces and confirmed increased p95 and 5xx; engaged SRE (oncall-inference)
07:52 UTC - Pulled GPU metrics and noticed high sustained utilization and elevated context-switch rates on node gpu-a100-1-12 in pool-rtp-03
08:05 UTC - Captured per-request histograms and saw long requests holding the CUDA stream for extended durations, blocking short ephemeral requests (head-of-line blocking)

08:20 UTC - Autoscaler logs indicate min_replicas=1 and a cooldown configured which prevented scale up despite sustained high utilization; scale up was suppressed due to cooldown policy from an earlier spike

08:35 UTC - Hypothesis formed: mis-sized autoscaler + mixed workload -> GPU serialization and kernel preemption leading to throughput collapse; noisy peer (another tenant in same pool) was running heavy long-seq batch jobs
08:50 UTC - Temporarily increased replicas to 3 and applied pod anti-affinity to separate the heavy job tenant; this immediately reduced p95 and cleared long queues
comments: Aisha Kaur (Support) 2026-03-10 07:50: Customer reports streaming disconnects; provided initial trace and ETA for first response: 30m
Daniel Park (SRE) 2026-03-10 08:02: Oncall pulled GPU telemetry; seeing high context-switch count on node gpu-a100-1-12. Suspect kernel preemption and workload mixing.
Ravi Mehta (Infra) 2026-03-10 08:30: Autoscaler cooldown prevented scale-up after earlier burst; min_replicas=1 is too low for known mixed workloads. Increasing replicas as a stopgap.
Scriptly-AI (Customer) 2026-03-10 08:40: Thanks — we see latency improving after your change. Please advise long-term mitigation.
hypothesis: The root cause is a combination of: 1) Autoscaler misconfiguration (min_replicas=1 + aggressive cooldown) that left the pool undersized for mixed long/short workloads; 2) GPU-level serialization when long-sequence requests and short chat requests share the same CUDA streams leading to kernel preemption/serialization and KV cache thrashing; and 3) a noisy peer in the same reservation running high-duration micro-batch jobs that exacerbated scheduling unfairness.
action_items: Hotfix (completed): increase dedicated pool replicas to 3 and add pod anti-affinity to isolate heavy-job tenant (2026-03-10 08:50 UTC)
Hotfix (completed): apply temporary rate-limiter at gateway for long-seq requests to smooth arrival rate for remainder of incident (2026-03-10 09:05 UTC)
Medium-term: update autoscaler policy for dedicated pools to set min_replicas >= 2 for mixed-workload reservations and reduce cooldown for scale_up evaluations
Medium-term: introduce per-tenant scheduling class for long-duration micro-batch jobs so we avoid interleaving on same GPU stream
Long-term: instrument per-stream kernel timings and add runtime heuristics to route long-requests to isolated GPU slices or variant models (quantized/faster)
resolution_summary: Applied emergency scale and anti-affinity which reduced p95 from 7.8s peak down to ~650ms within 12 minutes. Implemented gateway rate-limiting for long-seq requests to prevent immediate reoccurrence. Follow-up work created to adjust autoscaler defaults for dedicated reservations and implement scheduling isolation for heavy micro-batch workloads. Customer confirmed recovery and we provided post-incident notes and proposed mitigations.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - Recovery observed; 504s fell to 0. 2026-03-11 - Autoscaler policy PR opened (link above). 2026-03-12 - Confluence runbook updated with dedicated-pool sizing guidance for mixed workloads.
